verdict.cause:
The screen is correct and the presenter scripts are out of date. Both §1 sections were written from the September evidence runs (biotech 948ef3ce98 and mdx 28ff5309b5, 2026-09-21; last edited e9545110b6, 2026-10-15). In those runs intake gave the programs the codes "CAMA" and "DMN5". Commit 89441213ac (2026-11-01, "Project codes keep a code a name already has (C2C-101), and drop label noise") changed baseCodeFrom in server/routes/c2c/project-intake.ts:283-327. A code word already in the name ("C2C-101") is now kept as the code, and a bracketed label ("[Demo · MDX]") is ignored. The comments at lines 288 and 309 describe the old CAMA and DMN5 output. Today's seed therefore produces C2C-101 and NEUR, and the scripts were never updated.

The header has no code badge, no ACTIVE badge and no PLANNING badge on purpose. bylineChips in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectHome.tsx:1719-1726 shows only filing, region and indication, plus status when it is not 'active' and priority when it is high or critical. The code shows in the top-bar breadcrumb and in the About card (ProjectHome.tsx:2293). Phase and Status show as About rows.

The Projects list has no "workstream" label. Its List view shows the column "Client type: Medical device & IVD", plus Stage "Planning" and Status "Active". So the reporter's statement that Active and Planning appear only in About is slightly wrong: they are also List-view columns.

I found three more stale claims in the same §1 sections that the reporter did not list:
(a) Both scripts list "Lifecycle" as a journey step (biotech-walkthrough.md:35-36, mdx-walkthrough.md:32-33). The bar shows only Plan, Evidence, Author, Review, Submit, Respond. ProjectHome.tsx:2091 records that 'lifecycle' names a removed tab.
(b) The mdx §1 product note (mdx-walkthrough.md:41-43) tells the presenter that Project home cannot show the device taxonomy (finding F9) and not to promise it. The MDX About card now shows Device class Class II, Product code QNX, Regulation 21 CFR 866.3985, Review panel Microbiology, Predicate K223456, and Device flags (Software / AI-ML · Cyber device · Clinical data submitted). verdict.cause:
I reproduced this from a fresh session: Demo access, then the rail entry for each program, which lands on the Author stage.

**What the screen shows**
- C2C-101:
  - The Documents list has 6 Drafts, Module 2.5 "In review" and the Protocol Synopsis "Frozen".
  - Directly under it, Module completion reads "Dossier readiness 0% · 0 of 72 sections approved or locked. · No editing copy of this filing yet. · 0 in review · 0 drafted".
  - Each of the 5 module rows repeats "No editing copy of this filing yet.", so the line appears 6 times in all.
  - The Filing card on the right of the same page says "Dossier readiness 0%" and "2 documents in review".
- NeuroPanel-Dx: the 510(k) Summary is "Approved", yet the card reads "0 of 31 sections approved or locked … 0 in review · 0 drafted". The line repeats 8 times (the lead plus 7 rows), and the Filing card again says "2 documents in review".

**Root cause**
1. Readiness counts only the filing's own sections. `readDossier` (server/services/c2c/dossier-read.ts:337-370) counts `c2c_document_sections` of the governed filing: doc_fa5274… for C2C-101 and doc_cbd33d… for MDX. Every one of those sections has status 'todo'. Those sections only move when an authoring document bound to the filing (its "editing copy") is saved or signed. That happens in server/services/c2c/commit-section-to-filing.ts and in the UPDATE at server/routes/authoring.router.ts:7419.
2. Since commit 31a5453861 (2026-11-01), a document is bound only when its create names the filing (server/services/authoring/authoring-documents.ts:89-91, 125-144). The demo seed never names it: scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/work-areas.mjs:548 posts `/api/authoring/docs` without `c2c_document_id`, and so do the other demo document creates. The authoring docs read confirms it: `c2c_document_id` is null on all 7 MDX documents and all 12 C2C-101 documents. So the filing has no editing copy and stays at 0%. The figure is accurate for the filing itself.
3. The screen never says that the documents listed just above are not counted.
   - `noCopyWords`, home variant (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectDossier.tsx:241), returns a bare "No editing copy of this filing yet." with no next step. The market variant does give one.
   - That line is printed once in the lead (`MarketCopy` :134 via `HomeCopy` :149) and again in every `ModuleRow` (:280).
   - Line :194 prints "0 in review · 0 drafted" without saying "sections". On the same page, the Filing card's status line (ProjectMarkets.tsx `ProjectStatusLine`/`reviewWords`) counts documents ("2 documents in review"). So two "in review" counts contradict each other on one page.
4. A related raw code: `SECTION_STATUS_LABELS` (ProjectDossier.tsx:121-124) has no 'todo' entry. Every row's "Section status" disclosure therefore prints the raw value "todo".

**Classification**
- Not environment: the same seed gives the same state on any machine.
- Not stale-walkthrough: biotech §1 states no readiness figure. But a buyer who hears "one governed dossier", and in §3 hears that the synopsis is frozen and signed, will see Module 5 at "0 of 8" and readiness at 0%.

I suggest medium-to-high severity: the numbers are honest, but the copy makes the page contradict itself.

verdict.demoWorkaround:
On C2C-101 and NeuroPanel-Dx, stop at the Documents list on the Author stage. Do not scroll down into "Module completion", and do not open a row's "Section status", which shows the raw word "todo". The Filing card's "Dossier readiness 0%" is visible on the first screen of every step, so prepare one line for it:

"Readiness counts the filing's own governed sections, which move only when the filing's editing copy is approved section by section. The working documents above — the frozen and signed synopsis, the 2.5 in review, the approved 510(k) Summary — have not been committed into the filing yet. verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh session: Demo access, then rail Projects, then the program, then Evidence. Each part of the finding has a different cause.

1. **Where the rows come from.** Every time the data room's first page is read, the server copies the organization's Quality records into that project's data room as `cre_evidence_sources` rows (origin `native_record_snapshot`). The call is `data-room-search.ts:134` → `syncQualityProjectSources` → `readQualityProjectEvidence` → `reconcileRecordSources` (`record-source.ts:60-120`). That is why the C2C-101 data room holds 14 Quality rows and one uploaded .txt, C2C-201 holds 6 and NeuroPanel-Dx holds 14.

2. **Raw titles come from the server code.**
   - `server/services/qms/project-evidence.ts:245` builds the title `Retained Quality document ${document_id} v${version}`. It uses the numeric id because the query at `:228-232` never selects the parent's `doc_number` or `title`.
   - `project-evidence.ts:277` looks for a name in `title`, `supplier_name`, `name`, `change_number`, `nc_number`, `audit_number`, `period`, then falls back to `id`. A `qms_change_links` row has none of those fields, so it shows as "Quality record relationship: 4", even though the row has a `linked_label` (for example "[Demo · Biotech] SOP-002 Change Control").

3. **Each program's change control shows up in the other programs.**
   - The change-control register treats `program_id IS NULL` as organization-wide (`project-evidence-queries.ts:21-22`; scope set at `project-evidence.ts:267`). Organization-wide rows go into every project, labelled "Organization context". That labelling is deliberate.
   - The demo seed created both change controls without a project: `scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-qms.mjs:89` and `packs/mdx-qms.mjs:64` send no `programId`, although `POST /api/mdx/qms/changes` accepts one (`server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:1225-1231`, through `admitBodyProject`).
   - Result: the [Demo · MDX] NP-100 change control and its 3 links appear in both biotech projects, and the biotech C2C-101 amendment appears in NeuroPanel-Dx.

4. **Error-looking text on almost every row.** These copied records are always stored with `originalFileAvailable: false` (`record-source.ts:87`).
   - `SourceImportDialog.tsx:22` turns that into "The original file is unavailable, so a working copy cannot be created." `ProjectHome.tsx:408-419` shows it under a greyed-out "Work on document" button.
   - Each row also reads "File · …" (`kindLabel`, `ProjectHome.tsx:384-392`) and has a "Review file removal" button (`DocumentDisposition.tsx:225`), though it is a database record, not a file.
   - "No accessible citations" (`ProjectHome.tsx:343`) and "retained version; current approval not asserted" (`project-evidence.ts:246`) are accurate, but they are internal wording.

5. **Records card.** It labels every source "Client document" because `ProjectRecords.tsx:48` prints `enumWords(source_type)`, and every data room row has `source_type='client_document'`.

6. **Not reproduced today:**
   - **"C2C-201 Records 0 vs Evidence 6".** Records and Evidence both show 6 now. The 0 only appears on a project's very first visit: the Records card loads before the Evidence data room read creates the rows, and it does not reload afterwards. The rows now exist for all three programs, so the presenter will not see this today.
   - **"None of the six source PDFs".** This is not a defect. The PDFs are Vault documents, and walkthrough §2 points at Vault, not at the Evidence data room. The script is not contradicted.

No 5xx responses, console errors or page errors came up on these screens.
verdict.minimalFix:
Four changes in four files, in order of value:

**(a) Readable titles: `server/services/qms/project-evidence.ts`**
- In `readRetainedVersions` (`:228-232`), add `d.doc_number, d.title AS document_title` to the SELECT.
- Keep those two values when `row` is replaced by the `SELECT v.*` re-read at `:237-240`, for example with `row={...body.rows[0], doc_number: identity.doc_number, document_title: identity.document_title}`.
- At `:245`, build the title as `${doc_number} ${document_title} v${version} — retained version`.
- At `:277`, put `row.linked_label ?? row.linked_ref` before `row.id` in the name lookup. Optionally rename the label at `:77` from 'Quality record relationship' to 'Change-control link'.
- Caveat: `reconcileRecordSources` compares only the text checksum and the receipt, not the title (`record-source.ts:77`). Rows already stored keep their old titles until the database is re-seeded or `NATIVE_RECORD_REVISION` is bumped. A bump supersedes every copied row, so do not do it before today's demo.

**(b) Change controls in the wrong projects: seed data**
- `scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-qms.mjs:89`: add `programId: ctx.programId` to the POST body.
- `scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx-qms.mjs:64`: add the NeuroPanel-Dx program id.
- `changePatch` (`server/routes/mdx-qms.ts:1133`) cannot change `programId`, so today's database only clears up after a fresh re-seed.
- Once a change control has its project, the other projects drop its row at read time; nothing needs deleting. `createNativeRecordAdmission` at `record-source.ts:170-173` returns 404 when the key is missing, and the list keeps only readable ids.

**(c) Rows that look like errors: client**
- In `ProjectHome.tsx` `SourceWorkButton` (`:408`), render nothing for a source whose `origin === 'native_record_snapshot'` (equivalently, it has `catalog.nativeRecord`) instead of a disabled button with the "original file is unavailable" text. A Quality record never has a file.
- In the same file, label such a row 'Quality record' rather than 'File' in `kindLabel`, and hide 'Review file removal' for these rows.

**(d) "Client document" in Records: `ProjectRecords.tsx:48`**
- Show 'Quality record' instead of `enumWords(source_type)` when the records route returns that origin. This needs the route to select `provenance->>'origin'`.

All four are display or seed changes. None changes the schema or a governed write.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session: Demo access, then the rail's "[Demo · Biotech] C2C-201 oral JAK1 inhibitor", then Author. The finding is real, but the reporter overstated it in one way. The visible lines contradict the CMC work area:
- Documents says "No documents in this project yet. Ask AnA in the box above to draft one."
- Module completion says "0 of 72 … 0 in review · 0 drafted" and "Module 3 · Quality (CMC) · 0 of 20 approved or locked".
- Every Module 3 section under its "Section status" disclosure is listed as the raw value "todo".
- Records says "Authoring documents · 0".
- One click away, the "Compose Module 3 in CMC / Module 3" door opens CMC / Module 3, which lists 21 drafted sections (3.1, 3.2.S.1–7, 3.2.P.1–8, 3.2.A.1–3, 3.2.R.1.US, 3.3).

The overstatement: the program page does show the CMC work, but only inside the closed "Artifact section status" disclosure at the bottom of Module completion. It reads "21 sections · 0 approved or locked · 0 in review · 21 draft", plus jargon saying these states are separate from document-section completion. A client sees "0 drafted" and "No documents" first.

Root cause: Module 3 status lives in two stores that never meet.
1. The project page reads only the filing outline.
   - Module completion and Dossier readiness use GET /api/c2c/projects/:id/dossier, which counts only c2c_documents/c2c_document_sections (DOSSIER_SECTIONS_SQL at server/services/c2c/dossier-read.ts:196-202).
   - The Documents list uses GET /api/authoring/docs?programId=, which counts authoring documents only. Captured response: documents [] count 0.
2. CMC composes Module 3 elsewhere.
   - Compile writes cmc_module3_sections (server/services/cmc/module3-compile.ts:426).
   - The convergence service writes concept2cure_artifacts (server/services/module3-convergence-service.ts:724-771).
   - Placement writes coauthor_documents and submission_leaves (server/services/cmc/place-module3-into-submission.ts).
   - No CMC code writes c2c_document_sections, so this outline stays at "todo" forever. It would still read 0 drafted after every section is approved and placed.

The dossier route does carry the artifact rollup (artifactReadiness, from server/services/c2c/dossier-artifact-read.ts), but the client renders it only in that closed disclosure (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectArtifactReadiness.tsx:82, mounted at ProjectDossier.tsx:336).

The seed makes C2C-201 CMC-only on purpose (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-work-content.mjs:137-158: no Vault, protocol or authoring content). It is the only demo program whose Module 3 composes, so the contradiction appears only there.

Severity: I would rate it medium, not high. Neither docs/demo/biotech-walkthrough.md nor docs/demo/mdx-walkthrough.md mentions C2C-201, so this is off-script. It is still one of the three demo programs in the rail, and CMC is a featured work area.
verdict.minimalFix:
For today, a copy-only client change; no data or server change.

1. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectHome.tsx
   - Line 1600: pass the existing `cmcComposes` prop on, as `<ProjectDocumentsBody … cmcComposes={cmcComposes} />`.
   - Line 1516: add `cmcComposes?: boolean` to ProjectDocumentsBody's props.
   - Line 1532: when `cmcComposes` is true, replace the empty-state text with: "No documents in the editor for this project yet. Module 3 is composed in CMC / Module 3; its drafted sections are listed under Module completion, Artifact section status." Keep the current copy otherwise.
   - Line 1548: apply the same wording to the "No filing documents…" branch.
2. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectArtifactReadiness.tsx:82
   - Render the disclosure open when the artifact rollup has sections. That means computing `const hasSections = !!artifacts && artifacts.sections !== null && artifacts.state !== 'no_artifacts'` before the return and writing `<details className="pj-more" data-testid="pj-artifact-status" open={hasSections}>`.
   - The "21 draft" summary is then visible without a click.
3. Optional polish: add `['todo', 'Not started']` to SECTION_STATUS_LABELS in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ProjectDossier.tsx:121-123, so the section lists stop printing the raw value "todo".

Update client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/projectHomeDocuments.test.tsx and projectHomePlan.test.tsx if they assert the old copy or a closed disclosure.

The real fix is a design decision for the CMC/S7–S12 lane, not today's work. Either the CMC section lifecycle (draft, approve, place) updates the filing's c2c_document_sections Module 3 rows, or dossier-read.ts counts cmc_module3_sections for the Module 3 row. That fix is high risk.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session. Steps: Demo access, then the rail entry "[Demo · MDX] NeuroPanel-Dx 510(k)", then the journey bar's Submit, then "Assemble the eSTAR". The last click goes to /concept2cure/device-510k?program=40c30ed7-…, and the page shows exactly what was reported. There is a warning banner, the raw line "Reduced openFDA fallback unavailable — openFDA device/510k.json unreachable: fetch failed", and two red role=alert panels, "Could not load predicate candidates" and "Could not load substantial-equivalence rows". Each panel has a Try again button. Clicking Try again sends the request again and gets another 503.

The cause has three layers.

(1) Trigger (environment): GET /api/predicate-intelligence/candidates and /se-matrix return 503 {"error":"Predicate Intelligence not configured","detail":"REVIEW_ADMIN_TOKEN is not set"}. That comes from requireConfigured in server/routes/predicate-intelligence.ts:108-116. Predicate intelligence runs as a separate Python sidecar that this repository does not contain (docs/operations/predicate-intelligence-shadow-service.md). Neither REVIEW_ADMIN_TOKEN nor SHADOW_SERVICE_URL appears in .env.example. So a demo machine built from this repo will almost certainly hit the same 503. The openFDA fallback fails because this host has no network path to openFDA. The message is built in server/services/integrations/openfda-device-client.ts:86. A networked host might reach openFDA. But even then the SE matrix panel has no fallback, and the candidate panel's red box disappears only if openFDA returns rows for the fictional product code QNX.

(2) Product defect (presentation): K510Surface reports one known state (predicate intelligence not configured) up to four times.
- The banner at client/src/concept2cure/mdx/surfaces/K510Surface.tsx:393 already shows on every predicate read error (condition: predicates.error && !predicates.rows).
- The DataGate at :491-503 still renders a red ErrorState for that same error.
- The SE-matrix DataGate at :669-676 renders a second red ErrorState.
- The raw server reason string is printed verbatim at :410-413.
- The retries cannot succeed, because the server is reporting missing configuration, not a passing failure. DataState (client/src/concept2cure/mdx/lib/dataState.ts) has no 'unavailable' state, so this case falls into the generic error path.

(3) Product defect (counts): the eSTAR panel says "38 sections · 18 blockers" (K510Surface.tsx:750). The project page says "0 of 31 sections approved or locked". The governed k510 document (outline fda-estar-510k-v1.1) has 38 rows: 7 group headings (A–G) and 31 leaf sections. The dossier read leaves out headings that hold other sections (server/services/c2c/dossier-read.ts:162-169, markCountedSections in server/services/c2c/section-content.ts:244). The UI says so: "Empty headings that hold other sections are not counted." The 510(k) panel's source, GET /api/510k/projects/:id/document-preview (server/routes/k510-document-preview.ts:56-68), drops the hierarchy. It always sends parentSectionId:null and level:null, and loadGovernedSectionRows (server/services/pathway-engines/estar/estar-content-leaves.ts:364-376) does not select parent_key. So useK510.ts:90/158-161 counts all 38 rows and flags the 5 required headings (A, B, C, D, E) as blockers. 13 blockers are real. The padStart at K510Surface.tsx:785 also labels headings "§0A", "§0B" and so on.

(4) Stale walkthrough, a separate issue: docs/demo/mdx-walkthrough.md:38 says "36 eSTAR sections". That was true for outline v1.0 when the script was written (commit 28ff5309b5, 2026-09-21). migrations/20261005c_k510_denovo_estar_outline_v1_1.sql (commit 7581f06562, 2026-10-11) added A9 (MDUFA user fee) and D6 (benefit-risk), which makes 38.

Severity: the page is not a scripted walkthrough step; §4 goes through Submission Center. But "Assemble the eSTAR" is the first action in the device project's Submit stage, and the project's suggested prompt "What does the eSTAR still need?" points the same way. A presenter showing the device journey is likely to click it. I would rate it medium-high rather than a blocker.
verdict.minimalFix:
Today's fix is presentation only, in one file: client/src/concept2cure/mdx/surfaces/K510Surface.tsx.
(a) Line 491: change `{predicatesState.status !== 'ready' &&` to `{predicatesState.status !== 'ready' && predicatesState.status !== 'error' &&`. The banner at 393-405 already reports exactly this error, so the red ErrorState only repeats it. Optionally add a small "Check again" tb-btn inside that banner that calls predicates.refresh.
(b) Lines 669-676: when predicateFallbackActive && seState.status === 'error', render a calm `<EmptyState icon={I.circle} title="No substantial-equivalence matrix yet" hint="The matrix is built by predicate intelligence, which is not reachable for this tenant (see the notice above)." />`, imported from '../../v2/dataConnect' as DataGate.tsx:28 does, instead of the DataGate. verdict.cause:
The screens work as designed. The presenter script is what's out of date. docs/demo/biotech-walkthrough.md §3 (lines 56-76) was written on 2026-09-21 (commit 948ef3ce98). At that point the editor was a catalog entry called "Document editor & authoring", it opened on the program-bound synopsis, and the two unbound demo documents were missing from its tree. Slice A.1 (commit 4626be1f9a, 2026-10-26) renamed the surface "The editor" (shared/constants/ui-surface-registry.ts:242). The surface has no rail entry (navTier 'project'), so the only way in is a project's Author step.

The Author door "Find or start a document in the editor" (STEP_DOORS.editor, client/src/concept2cure/v2/projectDoors.ts:24; ProjectHome.tsx:1569-1572 and 1586-1589) clears any editor target on purpose and opens "the editor's own view, with no document named". With no target set, DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1391-1396 picks docs[0]. The list comes from GET /api/authoring/docs, which is ordered by updated_at DESC (server/services/authoring/authoring-document-read.ts:110). The seed runs ensurePlanDocuments after ensureAuthoring (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech.mjs:315), and the last plan document it creates is "Quality Overall Summary". That empty 23-section 2.3 QOS scaffold is therefore always the newest document, and it is what opens first.

The lock notes on a frozen document use the neutral .scaf-note style (background rgb(240,238,230)), not red. The editor tree now lists every document bound to the program: 5 plan documents, 4 SOPs, the IB summary, Module 2.5 and the synopsis, 12 in all. The script's "Known limit" note (evidence README finding 2) no longer holds.

verdict.demoWorkaround:
Don't look for "Document editor & authoring" in the rail or in Search; it doesn't exist. Avoid the "Find or start a document in the editor" link at the top of the list, which lands on the empty 2.3 QOS scaffold ("Write the section content here").

Don't say the other two documents are missing from the tree: Module 2.5 and the IB Summary are both in the editor's left-hand list and open with one click.

The adjacent note above it reads "Editing is refused while the document's status is FROZEN.", with the raw ALL-CAPS enum (from server/services/authoring/authoring-document-read.ts:41). If a client notices it, call it the system's status code.

verdict.cause:
The screen is honest. The data behind it is wrong for the story the presenter tells, and the cause is the demo seed code, not the runtime.

In scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-authoring.mjs, ensureComment (line 60) posts every comment with the author's session:
- line 66: `api('POST', /api/authoring/sections/:id/comment)`
- line 72: resolves them with the same session: `api('PATCH', /api/authoring/comments/:id)`

The second identity (ctx.signer, "Quinn Signer", oq-signer@validation.local) is in the same ctx (biotech.mjs:287/296). It is used for the review request, the freeze and the e-signature, but never for the comments. So both synopsis threads (S.2, S.5) were raised and resolved by founder@demo.local, the document's author, who is also the presenter.

The IB comment (biotech-content.mjs:302) is also posted by the author. Its body starts "Medical monitor: …", so the role exists only as text inside a record that names Demo Founder.

Separately, the raw email in "Resolved by founder@demo.local" is a small product inconsistency:
- Comment creation stores the person's name (server/routes/authoring.router.ts:2492, resolveSignerName).
- The PATCH resolve path stores `req.user?.email` as resolved_by (authoring.router.ts:2634).
- The editor's comments rail prints resolved_by as-is (client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DocumentWorkbench.tsx:6573-6575).

So the same person shows as "Demo Founder" on the thread and as an email on its resolution.

Re-running the seed on today's database does not repair it. ensureComment (line 64) matches existing rows by body alone, so the founder-authored rows are "found" and kept. Only a fresh database would pick up a seed fix.

verdict.cause:
The finding is real, and I reproduced it from a fresh browser session. I signed in with Demo access, then went C2C-101 → Author → Open on "[Demo · Biotech] Protocol Synopsis C2C-101-201".

The left rail shows "Saved draft sections · unbound" and the note "Unbound working copy. These sections belong to the saved draft…". The masthead next to it shows a "Frozen" chip, and the canvas says "This document is frozen. Its content is sealed under a content hash … this one remains the record."

The same happens on the Approved SOP-001. Its rail also says "Saved draft sections · unbound" and "Unbound working copy". The hidden project line in the rail header ends in "· Unbound draft", but at 1440px it is cut off by the ellipsis and not visible.

Root cause:
- `unboundDraft` (client/src/concept2cure/v2/editor/DocumentWorkbench.tsx:1736) is true whenever the binding is known and `binding.documentId === null`. `workingFilingBinding` (editor/filingSectionTarget.ts:25-33) returns that whenever the document's `c2c_document_id` is null.
- The document's status plays no part. In the seed, every authoring document in C2C-101 has `c2c_document_id: null`. The API confirms it for the synopsis: GET /api/authoring/docs/021f3bdd… returned status FROZEN with c2c_document_id null. The project has no editing copy of its home filing yet (the rail offers "Create editing copy"). So every document, frozen or approved ones included, gets the draft wording.
- The copy branches only on `unboundDraft`, never on `docSealed` (defined at :1755 as status FROZEN or APPROVED). The affected lines are:
  - :4368, the line under the title;
  - :4390, the shaded note;
  - :4347 and :5127, the "Unbound draft" module word.
- "Unbound", meaning not placed in a filing, is factually true. "Draft" and "working copy" are false for a sealed record.
- For the QMS SOPs, the note's advice to place the document into a filing also conflicts with the project page, which says quality documents "are not part of the filing".

)}` 3. Lines 4347 and 5127 (moduleWord and the masthead): change `'Unbound draft'` to `(docSealed ? 'Not in a filing' : 'Unbound draft')`. Why the risk is low: - No logic, binding or outline behaviour changes. - The tests that pin the current strings all use documents with status 'draft', so they keep passing unchanged: outlineStartsSection.test.tsx:155/168, filingSectionTarget.test.tsx:85, authoringConversationHandoff.test.tsx:157 and documentAuthoringEditor.test.tsx:145-149. - Add one test case with status 'FROZEN' that expects the new wording. verified.title: The release-signature gate reads 'Satisfied' with a check mark on an unsigned, unfrozen 510(k) sequence
verified.steps: 1. Open the program. 2. Use Search, type 'readiness' and open 'Readiness'. The same card appears on the project's Submit step under 'Rule detail'. 3. Look at the fourth gate card.
verified.observed: The card reads: check mark, 'A valid release signature binds this sequence's package (21 CFR 11.70) — Satisfied. RELEASE_SIGNATURE_VALID'. Sequence 0000 is still assembling. It has no package, no freeze and no signature. The API (GET /api/submissions/sequences/2/dispatch-readiness) returns releaseSignature {required:false, verdict:'unsigned', detail:'no orchestrator run is linked to this submission; and no dispatch-intent signature is recorded on ectd-sequence:2', cleared:true}.
verified.expected: For a 510(k), the gate should say that a release signature is not required for this submission type and that none exists. It should not show a check mark and 'Satisfied' for a 21 CFR 11.70 binding that does not exist. A Part 11-literate buyer will catch this.
verified.codePath: server/services/ectd/dispatch-gate.ts:196-198 (`if (!input.required) return { cleared: true, blockers: [] }`, with no reason); server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:240-252 (dispatchGateViews attaches `notAssessed` only when the caller passes it, and the release-signature gate is given none); client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/DispatchReadiness.tsx:83 (GateOutcome renders 'Satisfied.' for any cleared gate without notAssessed)
verified.suggestedFix: When required=false and verdict is not 'signed', return a notAssessed-style statement, for example 'Not required for a 510(k); no release signature exists'. Render it the way the external-validation gate's 'Not assessed' is rendered, the same pattern as the externalNotAssessed fix of 2026-09-28.
verified.walkthroughLine: §5 Point at: "Cleared to dispatch? — Dispatch blocked" … The verdict source is the deterministic assessment

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh Playwright session: Demo access, then the rail's "[Demo · MDX] NeuroPanel-Dx 510(k)", then Submit and "Rule detail". I also reached it through rail Search, typing 'readiness' and opening Readiness. On both screens the fourth gate card (li[data-gate="releaseSignature"], class "dr2-gate ok") shows a check mark, "A valid release signature binds this sequence's package (21 CFR 11.70)" and "Satisfied." The sequence behind it is 0000, still assembling, with 7 leaves. The live response from GET /api/submissions/sequences/2/dispatch-readiness has releaseSignature {required:false, verdict:'unsigned', detail:'no orchestrator run is linked to this submission; and no dispatch-intent signature is recorded on ectd-sequence:2', cleared:true}. Its gates[3] is {key:'releaseSignature', cleared:true} with no notAssessed.

Root cause:
1. server/services/ectd/release-signature-status.ts:72-78 limits the required types to IND, NDA, BLA and MAA, so a 510(k) is not required.
2. server/services/ectd/dispatch-gate.ts:196-198 returns { cleared: true, blockers: [] } whenever required is false. It gives no reason, so "not required and unsigned" looks the same as "signed and verified".
3. server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:1002-1006 builds the notAssessed map for dispatchGateViews. It has entries for external, structural (IND clinical hold) and shadowPresence (waiver), but none for releaseSignature. So dispatchGateViews (lines 240-252) attaches no note.
4. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/DispatchReadiness.tsx:83 (GateOutcome) and :114-118 (GateCard) then draw any cleared gate without notAssessed as a check mark and "Satisfied." The card title is the corpus rule's title (server/services/ectd/validation-rule-corpus.ts:658), which states that a valid signature binds the package. That is false for this sequence.

This is the same misreport the codebase already fixed for the external validator (externalNotAssessed, assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:255-273: "advisory is not passed"), not yet applied to this gate. Only submission types outside IND/NDA/BLA/MAA are affected, so the demo's 510(k) is. The biotech INDs are not, because there the gate is required and blocks.

The walkthrough does not claim this card is satisfied. mdx-walkthrough.md §5 points only at "Dispatch blocked" with two blockers, and the screen does show "Dispatch blocked · 2 blockers". So this is not a stale-walkthrough finding. But the card sits in plain view right under the presenter's pointer.

Separate observation, outside this finding: the rest of mdx-walkthrough.md §5 is stale. It says 6 leaves, six error-severity UNRESOLVED_DOCUMENT findings and F5. The screen shows 7 leaves, 0 errors and 10 warnings, and the structural blocker is "7 leaves point at documents not yet approved".
verdict.minimalFix:
Change one file on the server: server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts, the notAssessed map passed to dispatchGateViews at lines 1002-1006. Add a releaseSignature note for the case where the signature is not required and none is recorded:

```ts
{
  external: externalNotAssessed(externalGate),
  ...(indProgram && { structural: indProgram.view.clinicalHold.note }),
  ...(shadowPresence.notAssessed && { shadowPresence: shadowPresence.notAssessed }),
  ...(!signatureRequired && releaseSignature.verdict !== 'signed' && {
    releaseSignature: `A ${submissionApplicationType ?? 'submission of this'} type does not require a 21 CFR Part 11 release signature before dispatch, so this gate does not block. No release signature is recorded for this sequence, so none binds its package.`,
  }),
},
```

The 'invalid' verdict already sets cleared:false (dispatch-gate.ts:185-194), and dispatchGateViews attaches a note only to cleared gates, so the tamper path is untouched. The client already handles a gate with a note:
- DispatchReadiness.tsx:83 and :114-118 render the warning icon with "Not assessed. <note>" instead of a check mark and "Satisfied."
- ProjectMarkets.tsx:83-85 and :159 list the gate on the Submit market row as "not assessed".
- DispatchReadiness.tsx:305-307 passes the note to AnA's context.

No change to the verdict or blockers is needed. Optionally, a later polish: let GateOutcome say "Not required for this submission type." rather than the generic "Not assessed." prefix.

Add one case to server/services/ectd/__tests__/assess-dispatch-readiness.gates.test.ts: dispatchGateViews given releaseSignature {cleared:true} with a releaseSignature note carries notAssessed. Per repo rules, the commit needs a Plan: and Completes: trailer naming assess-dispatch-readiness.ts.
verdict.demoWorkaround: On the Submit step, do not expand "Rule detail: gates, findings and the rules behind them". On the Readiness screen, point only at the "Dispatch blocked · 2 blockers" header and the two red cards, and do not scroll to the fourth card. If the client asks about it, say: "For a 510(k) this product's gate does not require a Part 11 release signature, and none exists yet. The card means not-required, not signed. The INDs, where it is required, show it as a blocker." Do not describe it as a satisfied 11.70 binding.
verdict.codePath: server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:1002-1006 (no releaseSignature note when the signature is not required); server/services/ectd/dispatch-gate.ts:196-198 (not required returns cleared with no reason); server/services/ectd/release-signature-status.ts:72-78 (required types are IND, NDA, BLA and MAA only); client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/DispatchReadiness.tsx:83 and :114-118 (a cleared gate without a note renders a check mark and "Satisfied."); server/services/ectd/validation-rule-corpus.ts:658 (the card title asserts a valid signature binds the package)

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session: Demo access, then the NeuroPanel-Dx program in the rail, then Submission Center, then the Builder tab. The Builder lists 7 leaves for sequence 0000. Six are at CTD codes (1.14, 1.16, 3.2.P.1, 3.2.R, 5.3.1.4, 5.3.5.2). The seventh is the same vault document as 3.2.P.1 ("[Demo · MDX] Device Description and Principles of Operation", vault uuid 434ce5c8…) placed again at section "estar.device-description". The History panel shows "Section estar.device-description · Leaf Created". Every row reads "Vault document · not yet determined", and a note above the table says "Source evidence not yet determined for 7 leaves". On the program's Submit step the card reads "Sequence 0000 · Assembling · 7 leaves" and lists the approval of that one document twice, once for estar.device-description and once for 3.2.P.1. The dispatch-readiness response gives leafCount 7.

The product is doing what it was designed to do. The walkthrough is out of date, and the demo seed leaves behind a test placement.

1) The walkthrough was written on 2026-09-21 (commit 28ff5309b5e). The next day, commit d0da50de06 ("The placement vocabulary follows the submission type") changed which section codes a 510(k) sequence accepts:
- submission-service.ts:4678-4697: upsertLeaf now checks the code against the vocabulary of the submission type.
- placement-vocabulary.ts:80-82: '510k' maps to the 'estar' vocabulary.
- placement-vocabulary.ts:335-355: that vocabulary only checks the code's shape (lower-case words joined by hyphens or dots).

So "estar.device-description" is accepted. The CTD codes pass only because they also fit that shape once lower-cased ("3.2.p.1"). The script's claims that "the leaf route only accepts CTD-shaped section codes" and that "an eSTAR section id is refused" have been false since 2026-09-22. The manifest also contradicts "the refusal is in the manifest": docs/evidence/DEMO/mdx/manifest.json records the estarLeafProbe with status 200 and its notes contain no F3 refusal.

2) The seed's probe step (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs:386-394) sends a real PUT to place a leaf. It used to throw on HTTP 200 with the message "revisit the pack". Commit c5170db97f (2026-10-31) changed line 391 to return success and leave the leaf in place. Nobody updated the walkthrough or removed the probe leaf. That is where the duplicate seventh leaf and the doubled approval blocker come from.

3) "Each pinned to its content hash" is true in the data but not visible on screen. Every leaf has documentContentSha256 set, and sourceDocument.pin is "match". But LeafSourceCell (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/SubmissionSeqWorkspaces.tsx:559-591) shows no chip when the source status is 'undetermined'; this was a deliberate change (D7-A2 step 9, see lines 579-582). So the presenter would be pointing at "not yet determined" while claiming the leaves are pinned. The only hashes in the Builder are the audit-record hashes in History.

The same leftover leaf also makes §5 stale: it says "6 leaves", but the screen and API say 7.

The "Device filings · eSTAR" card ("nothing assemblable yet · 11 required sections missing") comes from /api/510k/estar/assemble and does not read leaves. It is consistent with the script's "not yet what this surface files into" and is not part of this defect.
verdict.minimalFix:
Two changes, both outside product code.

(A) Remove the probe from the demo seed. In scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs, delete lines 386-394, the run.step('Submission Center: eSTAR section codes on the leaf route (probe)', …) block. If the probe is kept, change it so it never leaves a placement behind. For example, on HTTP 200 immediately DELETE /api/submissions/sequences/${out.sequence.id}/leaves/${r.json.id} with a reason; the sequence is still in draft at that point. Simply deleting the step is cleaner.

Note that the seed is idempotent and never removes existing leaves. Databases that are already seeded, including today's, keep the seventh leaf until they are re-seeded from a clean database or the leaf is removed in the Builder.

verdict.cause:
The finding is real, and the fault is in the script, not the screen. Walkthrough §5 (docs/demo/mdx-walkthrough.md:128-147) and evidence finding F5 (docs/evidence/DEMO/mdx/README.md:82-83, 137-151, 210-212) describe the build of 2026-09-21. Commit f41a06298d fixed F5 the same day the pack and walkthrough were written ("WP: a vault-filed leaf resolves, so a sequence built from the vault can clear the gate"). Since then, hasCompleteDocumentPointer (server/services/ectd/dispatch-readiness.ts:488-503) treats a vault_documents leaf as complete when it carries its uuid; the file's own header note at lines 17-21 records the old integer-only check. The vault-backed leaves now resolve. contentFindings (dispatch-readiness.ts:525-569) then correctly raises DOCUMENT_NOT_APPROVED: a warning with blocksRelease:true, from founder decisions FD5 and P-22, because none of the seeded vault documents is approved. The live gate is therefore "7 leaves point at documents not yet approved" plus "no Shadow Review". It reports 0 errors and 10 warnings (7 × DOCUMENT_NOT_APPROVED, 3 × MISSING_REQUIRED_SECTION for 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3), and UNRESOLVED_DOCUMENT appears nowhere. That is correct, fail-closed behaviour.

The 7th leaf is also a stale-script effect. The seed pack probes the leaf route with an eSTAR section id (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs:386-391). The route's upsertLeafSchema (server/routes/submissions.ts:231-233) now accepts any sectionCode of 1-64 characters, so the probe returns 200. The pack keeps that leaf ("the CTD placements below stay as well"), which leaves the Device Description placed twice: at estar.device-description and at 3.2.P.1. So §4's "six leaves" and "an eSTAR section id is refused (finding F3)" are stale too.

Naming: the page at /concept2cure/dispatch-readiness is headed "Submission readiness" (the P-33 name). It has no rail entry and no "Cleared to dispatch?" line. That line exists only on Submission Center > Dispatch (SubmissionSeqWorkspaces.tsx:2201-2231), which reads "Not yet. Two things stand between sequence 0000 and dispatch." §5's PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE dispatch-QC remark is also not visible on the readiness page; it would appear only after "Run dispatch QC" on the Dispatch tab.

When the MDX demo pack was written (commit 28ff5309b5), its seed recorded a training acknowledgement of SOP-101 for the seed identity (POST /api/mdx/qms/documents/:id/training-ack with method 'attestation'). The walkthrough line and the evidence README were written to match that seed. A read-and-understood acknowledgement became a personal attestation that only the signed-in human can make (docs/architecture/QMS_PERSONAL_TRAINING.md). The seed step was rewritten so it only checks readiness and records executed:false, with the note "Demo setup does not attest for the reader" (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx-qms.mjs:122-135). verdict.cause:
I reproduced this from a fresh session. I signed in with Demo access, opened [Demo · MDX] NeuroPanel-Dx 510(k) from the rail, then opened Submission Center. On the default Submissions tab, the Device filings · eSTAR card shows one action: 'Open the 510(k) filing panel'. Clicking it opens /concept2cure/device-510k?program=40c30ed7-…. Project > Submit > 'Assemble the eSTAR' opens the same screen. What appears there, part by part:

(1) Two red errors with 'Try again' (the main defect). The server answers 503 to GET /api/predicate-intelligence/candidates and /se-matrix with {"error":"Predicate Intelligence not configured","detail":"REVIEW_ADMIN_TOKEN is not set"} (server/routes/predicate-intelligence.ts:107-115, requireConfigured). That service is an external Python sidecar (docs/operations/predicate-intelligence-shadow-service.md). Its source is not in this repo, and neither the demo seed nor the launch scripts set SHADOW_SERVICE_URL or REVIEW_ADMIN_TOKEN. So any demo instance built from this repo is missing it, not only this machine. K510Surface already recognises the state and shows an amber banner (K510Surface.tsx:393-405). It then also draws DataGate error panels for candidates (lines 486-502) and for the SE matrix (lines 669-736). DataGate.tsx:160-170 renders every error, including a known 'not configured' 503, as a red 'Could not load {label}' with a retry that can never succeed. So one known missing service is reported three times, twice in red.

(2) 'Reduced openFDA fallback unavailable — openFDA device/510k.json unreachable: fetch failed'. This one comes from the machine: node fetch to api.fda.gov fails with ENOTFOUND here, and curl gets proxy 403. The raw 'fetch failed' wording is passed through unchanged, built at server/services/integrations/openfda-device-client.ts:86 and printed at K510Surface.tsx:412. That wording is a product polish issue.

(3) All eSTAR sections 'empty' is an honest state, not a defect. GET /api/510k/projects/:id/document-preview returns doc_cbd33d8…, docType k510, 38 sections, every one status todo with contentLength 0. That is the governed eSTAR document intake scaffolded. The approved 510(k) Summary lives in authoring_documents with sections '1'-'9', and the seed never put it into §A5. The Submission Center card itself says '11 required sections missing', and the seeded task says 'Close the eSTAR sections still missing required content'. One small mismatch: the screen says 38 sections, while walkthrough §1 says 36.

(4) The missing space before 'Withdraw' is a CSS fault. The Withdraw button uses className 'tb-btn' (K510Surface.tsx:448-456), which app-v2.css:1770 fixes at width:32px;height:32px as an icon button. The 10px word 'Withdraw' (about 45px wide) overflows the 32px box on both sides, eats the 6px margin and sits flush against ')'. Measured box: 32x32 at x=696.

(5) 'SepsiScreen Panel (demo predicate)' is a seed inconsistency. It is set at scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs:70, while mdx-content.mjs:121 describes the predicate as 'a legally marketed cartridge-based multiplex CNS pathogen panel'.

On the walkthrough: §4 tells the presenter to go to Sequences → Builder and never says to open this panel, so no Say line is contradicted. But the button is the only action on the Submission Center landing view where §4 starts, so a presenter or the client can easily click it.

verdict.cause:
Two validators judge the same sequence 0000, and neither tells the user it is only one of the two.

(1) The Dispatch, Validation and Readiness screens read assessSequenceDispatchReadiness (server/services/ectd/assess-dispatch-readiness.ts:832-874). It checks Module 1 sections required by the region profile (requiredModule1Codes, :617) and IND Module 3 (originalModule3Requirement), plus IND-program and company-legal findings. For seed sequence 1 that comes to 8 errors: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.12.14, 1.14.4.2, 1.20, 3.2.S and 3.2.P. It also gives 6 DOCUMENT_NOT_APPROVED warnings. It never reads the package identity (application number, bound sponsor, D-U-N-S, regulatory contact).

(2) Compile & export's Validate (server/routes/ectd-compile.ts:1579-1650) works differently:
- It prepends packageIdentityFindings (:420-436), which gives 4 PACKAGE_IDENTITY_MISSING errors. The seed records no application number or sponsor; Forms and letters shows "No sponsor bound".
- It then runs leafPlacementFindings (:955) against resolveRequiredSections, which reads rule pack ind:fda ich-m4-v2.2. That pack marks 36 leaf sections mandatory: all of Module 2 (with 2.3.S and 2.3.P separately, so the QOS leaf at 2.3 does not count), 12 sections of 3.2.S/3.2.P and 6 of 4.2.x. That is 33 missing sections, so 37 errors in all.
- It does not report the 6 unapproved documents.

The header of server/services/ectd/required-sections.ts:1-20 says it is "ONE resolver for every gate", written to stop compile and readiness disagreeing. But the dispatch gate does not use it. That is the duplication the header says it closed.

The understatement on Dispatch is real too. The freeze and dispatch acts run governedContentGates (server/services/submission-service/submission-service.ts:1939-1959). That function first runs the 4-blocker gate and then assertSequencePackageable. At :1876 assertSequencePackageable refuses on missing package identity with "Nothing can be frozen or dispatched." The Dispatch headline counts only a.gate.blockers (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/SubmissionSeqWorkspaces.tsx:2201-2217). So "Four things stand between sequence 0000 and dispatch" leaves out the identity gaps, which the act itself would refuse on. Clearing those four things would show "Yes, cleared" and then the signed freeze would still be refused. I took this from the code; I did not complete a freeze to prove it.

C2C-201 has no sequence, so only C2C-101 shows this.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session: Demo access, then rail C2C-101, then rail Submission Center, then the Sequences, Validation and Dispatch tabs. Every claim in the finding shows on screen. No 4xx/5xx, console or page errors occurred, and GET /api/submissions/1/module2-qc returned 200 in about 94 ms.

There are four separate root causes.

(1) The panel grades only summaries the platform builds itself, but its wording says "missing".
- server/services/authoring/module2-saved-qc.ts:68-115 builds 2.3 only from approved, composed CMC sources (composeFullModule3, then buildM23QualityOverallSummary). It builds 2.5 and 2.7 only from completed CSR builds, and never builds 2.4.
- At line 112 it passes `expectedSummaries: [...DEFAULT_EXPECTED_M2]`, which is ['2.3','2.4','2.5','2.7'] (m2-summary-qc.ts:28). It applies this to every application type, including an original US IND, which 21 CFR 312.23 does not require to carry CTD 2.5 or 2.7.
- runM2SummaryQc (m2-summary-qc.ts:89-98) therefore emits severity 'error', code PRESENCE, "Expected Module 2 summary 2.3 is missing."
- It never reads the sequence's leaves. So the vault-placed "Quality Overall Summary — C2C-101" leaf at m2.3, which the same Validation tab lists two panels above, is invisible to it.

(2) The panel calls these rows "Blocking", but nothing blocks on them.
- The client maps every 'error' to a red "Blocking" chip (SubmissionModule2Qc.tsx:93).
- No gate consumes this QC. The only consumers of readSavedModule2Qc/runM2SummaryQc are the GET route (server/routes/submissions.ts:1404-1424) and this panel.
- The Dispatch tab's verdict ("Four things stand between sequence 0000 and dispatch") lists no Module 2 item.

(3) The 2.3 reason is the export gate's generic fallback, and it is untrue here.
- C2C-101 is a biologic. The seed deliberately compiles no Module 3 for it (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech.mjs:306-313: "C2C-101's build is refused by the boundary").
- With totalSections = 0, evaluateFinalExportGate falls through to 'Critical contradictions or missing approvals block final export' (server/services/cmc/final-export-gate.ts:383).
- module2-saved-qc.ts:82-83 shows that text verbatim. There are no contradictions; the real reason is that this product does not compose a biologic's Module 3. The composition-scope check in load-approved-cmc-sources-for-project.ts:133-150 runs only after the gate passes, so its honest reason never appears.

(4) Copy problems.
- The internal ID "(founder decision R-1)" is hard-coded at module2-saved-qc.ts:97.
- The raw code "PRESENCE" is rendered at SubmissionModule2Qc.tsx:94.
- "build(s)" is at SubmissionModule2Qc.tsx:82.
- Each reason is printed twice: once in its row (line 97) and again in the "Not built now" footer (lines 106-110).

The API response confirms all of this: checked [], missingSummaries ['2.3','2.4','2.5','2.7'], counts.errors 4, cmcGate 'closed', module3Sections 0. The heading meanwhile reads "nothing built to check".

The panel is not on a scripted walkthrough step; script steps 5 and 6 are Sequences and Dispatch. It sits on the Validation tab between them, and the script has the presenter say "QOS at 2.3". If the client scrolls, the panel says 2.3 is missing and blocking. I would rate it medium-high, not a blocker.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh session (Demo access, then the rail's C2C-101, then Submit, then "See every sequence in Submission Center", then "Forms and letters", which opens /concept2cure/ind-checklist). The finding has three separate causes.

(1) Placed Vault leaves are ignored. In server/services/ind-lifecycle/ind-checklist-view-assembler.ts, placedDocuments() (lines 423-441) skips every leaf that is not a coauthor_documents leaf (line 427: `if (l.document_table !== 'coauthor_documents' || l.document_id == null) continue;`). In the seeded database, all 6 leaves of C2C-101 sequence 0000 are vault_documents leaves (keyed by document_uuid): m1.14.4.1, m5.3.5.1 twice, m2.3, m2.6.6 and m1.6.3. So statusByCode is empty, and evaluateIndReadiness treats every code as 'not_started'. The page then shows "m1.14.4.1 — Investigator's Brochure -- Not started", "m2.3 ... Not started" and "m2.6.6 ... Not started". The assembler's own rule says not_started "means no doc" (comment at line 112), yet a document is placed at each of these codes. The Vault documents have status 'pending' and no canonical_documents stage, so 0% approved is correct. "Not started" is not.

(2) The module cards claim "required" for a set that is not the required set. getModuleProgress (services/regulatory/ind-ectd-sections.ts:2264-2293, called from ind-readiness-service.ts:200) counts every leaf or estimated-hours section in the blueprint: 18/29/17/20/12, 96 in total. The client labels each card "{completed}/{total} required sections approved" (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/IndLifecycle.tsx:1386). The real required set, used by the headline and the blockers, is 48 (by module: M1 13, M2 9, M3 15, M4 9, M5 2). I confirmed these counts by running the pure functions.

(3) Two screens use different required sets. Compile's Module readiness reads rule pack ind:fda ich-m4-v2.2 (36 required, counted by placement) and shows "3 of 36 required sections placed" and "Clinical Study Reports 1/1, 100%, Ready" in green. On the same Submission Center, the checklist reads the 108-section blueprint (48 required, counted by approval) and shows Module 5 at 0% and m5.3.5 as Not started. The reporter's fourth number is overstated: the Planner's "Required Module 1 for IND · 9" agrees with Compile's Administrative Information "1/9". So there are three inconsistent figures (36, 48 and a mislabelled 96), not four.

Two related points. m5.3.5 and m1.14 read "Not started" partly because the blueprint marks 19 heading codes as required (m1-m5, m2.3, m5.3.5 and others), and nothing rolls child sections up to them. The fix in (1) does not cover those headings. Neither walkthrough visits Forms and letters, so no presenter line is contradicted directly. But step 5 of the script has the presenter say the IB, QOS and tox summary are placed at 1.14.4.1, 2.3 and 2.6.6, and this page says Not started for exactly those codes.
verdict.minimalFix:
Two display-only changes are safe for today. Neither changes a readiness verdict, percentage or blocker count. I checked this with evaluateIndReadiness: overall stays 0% and blockers stay 51; only the three statuses change from not_started to drafting.

A) Correct the card label. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/IndLifecycle.tsx:1386, change `{m.completed}/{m.total} required sections approved` to `{m.completed}/{m.total} sections approved`. getModuleProgress counts all 96 blueprint sections, not the 48 required ones. A more thorough option is to compute the cards over the required set in ind-readiness-service.ts:198-200, so each card's total matches the headline's 48. That option is still low risk, but it changes numbers the existing tests may pin.

B) Treat placed Vault leaves as placed, not approved. In server/services/ind-lifecycle/ind-checklist-view-assembler.ts placedDocuments() (lines 423-441), before the coauthor-only `continue` on line 427, add a branch: if `l.document_table === 'vault_documents' && l.document_uuid` and the sequence maps to a submission, call `put(m, sectionKey(str(l.section_code)), 'drafting', '')`. Keep the leaf out of formDocsBySub. Never map it to approved/signed/locked here, because approval of a Vault version is a separate gate (vaultVersionNotTransmittable and the P-95 quorum). The three sections then read "Drafting" instead of "Not started", and the Module 1, 2 and 5 cards show an item in progress. Also update the header comment at lines 22-28, which says sections come only from coauthor leaves. Counting an approved Vault version as approved, and converging the 36 (rule pack) and 48 (blueprint) required sets onto one source, are larger changes and should not go in on demo day.
verdict.demoWorkaround: Stay on the script: neither walkthrough opens "Forms and letters" (the IND forms checklist), so do not click it in Submission Center. If filing readiness comes up, use Compile & export's Module readiness ("3 of 36 required sections placed in sequence 0000") and Dispatch readiness, which the script already covers. If the checklist does get opened, describe it as approval-based: "0 of 48 required sections are approved; the six Vault documents are placed but still pending review." Do not read out the "Not started" chips or the module cards' "required sections approved" figures (0/18, 0/29, 0/17, 0/20, 0/12). Also avoid pointing at Compile's green "Clinical Study Reports 1/1 Ready" next to this page: it counts placement, not approval.

None is a coauthor_documents leaf. The matching vault.documents rows (IB, protocol, SAP, CMC QOS, tox summary, pre-IND minutes) all have status 'pending' and no canonical_documents stage, so they are placed but not approved.

verdict.cause:
The finding is real, and I reproduced it from a fresh browser session. All six biotech PDFs in the Vault show literal "?" characters, and the title and subtitle lines run off the right edge of the page.

Steps I took: signed in with Demo access, clicked the rail entry "[Demo · Biotech] C2C-101 …", then rail Vault > Uploads · 6 > each document > Versions > View. The in-app viewer loads GET /api/c2c/project-vault/7f7bc7b2-…/documents/<id>/download (200, application/pdf) into a blob iframe. I saved those served bytes and checked them:
- The IB's SHA-256 is b23339ccea9d…, the same hash the Vault record shows. These are the governed bytes, not a rendering artefact.
- The "?" is a literal 0x3F byte in the PDF content stream, so every viewer (Chrome, Acrobat, pdftotext) shows "?".

What the documents show:
- **IB:** "Edition 3.0 ? C2C-101 … ? Concept2Cure Therapeutics (fictio" (cut off), "2?8 °C", "14?18 days", "30?300 mg", and the footer "DEMO ? fictional content ? …" on every page.
- **Protocol:** "PASI ? 12, BSA ? 10 %", "sPGA ? 3", "Adults 18?75 years", "(? 90 kg, > 90 kg)", "Day ?28 to ?1". Its 16 pt title, "… v1.0 ? Phase 2, randomized, pla", is cut off at the page edge too.
- **SAP:** "Cochran?Mantel?Haenszel", "Miettinen?Nurminen", "Kaplan?Meier".
- **QOS:** "IgG1? monoclonal antibody", "Fc? receptor", "monomer ? 98.5 %", "stored at ?70 °C", "pH (5.7?6.3)".
- **Tox and Pre-IND minutes:** "?" in place of every dash, for example "Question 1 ? Nonclinical package".

The Vault search shows it as well. Searching "Investigator" in the C2C-101 Vault selects the IB, and the detail panel's text excerpt reads "DEMO ? fictional content ? Concept2Cure Therapeutics | Page 1 of 2 … Edition 3.0 ? C2C". That excerpt is extracted from the same PDF bytes.

Root cause, all in the demo seed's PDF builder, `scripts/demo/launch-demo/lib.mjs`:
1. **The "?" characters.** `pdfLatin1()` (lines 250-257) runs `.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e\xa0-\xff]/g, '?')` on every string. The biotech content (`packs/biotech-content.mjs`) uses these characters, which all hit that rule: — (34), – (27), ≥ (14), ≤ (6), − (5), κ and γ. The footer at `packs/biotech.mjs:201` is "DEMO — fictional content — …". The fonts are declared `/WinAnsiEncoding` (lines 314-315), and that encoding does contain the en dash (0x96), em dash (0x97) and curly quotes, but the function never maps to them.
   - The MDX pack is clean because `packs/mdx.mjs:107-110` passes everything through its own `latin1()` (`packs/mdx-shared.mjs:16`), which turns —/– into "-" and ≥/≤ into ">="/"<=" first. The biotech pack (`biotech.mjs:201`) does not.
2. **The overflow.** `makeMultiPagePdfBuffer` pushes the title (16 pt bold, line 293) and subtitle (11 pt, line 294) as single lines without wrapping. Only body paragraphs go through `wrap(p, 88)`. Every biotech subtitle in `biotech-content.mjs` (lines 42, 76, 120, 162, 193, 229) is longer than the 468 pt column, so it is cut off at the right edge.

It is not an environment issue. Any database seeded by this script gets these bytes, and the seed never replaces a document it finds by title (`biotech.mjs` ensureVaultDoc: `if (hit) tally.found(...)`). The walkthrough line (biotech §2: "Optionally open the IB: it is a real two-page document, not a placeholder") is literally true, since the file is real and two pages long. But the document a regulated buyer would read is visibly corrupted.

Side note, outside this finding: the search excerpt starts "Demo · Biotech] …", with the leading "[" dropped.

verdict.minimalFix:
Two changes, both in the demo seed `scripts/demo/launch-demo/lib.mjs`. Nothing the product runs at request time changes.

(1) In `pdfLatin1` (lines 250-257), map the common characters before the catch-all `?` rule. The fonts already use WinAnsiEncoding and the body is written with `Buffer.from(body, 'latin1')`, so the WinAnsi code points render as real dashes and quotes:
```js
.replace(/–/g, '\x96').replace(/—/g, '\x97')
.replace(/‘/g, '\x91').replace(/’/g, '\x92')
.replace(/“/g, '\x93').replace(/”/g, '\x94')
.replace(/•/g, '\x95').replace(/…/g, '\x85')
.replace(/≥/g, '>=').replace(/≤/g, '<=').replace(/−/g, '-')
.replace(/→/g, '->').replace(/κ/g, 'kappa').replace(/γ/g, 'gamma')
```
The existing `.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e\x91-\x97\x85\xa0-\xff]/g, '?')` stays last, with its class widened to keep the mapped bytes. To be maximally conservative, map – and — to '-' instead, as `mdx-shared.mjs:16` does.

(2) In `makeMultiPagePdfBuffer`, wrap the title and subtitle as the body already is. Change lines 293-294 to:
```js
for (const l of wrap(title, 52)) push(l, true, 16);
if (subtitle) for (const l of wrap(subtitle, 88)) push(l, false, 11);
```
The running header at 8 pt (line 323) fits as it is.

How the fix takes effect: the seed never re-ingests a document it finds by title, and Vault versions are immutable. So the change only reaches a freshly seeded database, or one where the biotech pack has been purged and re-seeded. It also changes the seeded PDFs' SHA-256, which nothing asserts: there are no tests on these bytes, and the found path records `contentHash: null`.

The change touches the demo seed only (lib.mjs is shared by the biotech, mdx, faux, lumen and lumen-vault packs). It is low risk in code. Re-seeding the live demo database hours before the demo is the riskier part.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced it from a fresh Demo access session. Path: rail Vault > "Open its Vault" on C2C-101 > Uploads · 6 > "Statistical Analysis Plan C2C-101-201 v1.0". The detail pane shows "Filed by: Demo Founder, 2026-11-09 16:58 UTC", "Looks like: Protocol", "CTD section: m5.3.5.1" and a grey note: "Filed into Module 5 (CTD m5.3.5.1) by the launch demo seed; placement confirmed by the founder's session." History lists only "Uploaded to the Vault" (16:58), "Filing recorded" (16:58) and later "Downloaded" rows. The MDX Analytical Performance Study Report shows "Filed by the MDX demo pack into k510. Provenance: seeded demonstration content … Not model-drafted — no AI provider is configured."

The reporter's central claim is wrong at the record level. A suggestion step did happen; the screen just hides it. I checked with a read-only SQL query (BEGIN READ ONLY) on audit_logs:
- chain_seq 7, vault.document.ingest: filing = {placementStatus:'suggested', folderId:'module-5', confidence:'medium', rationale:'Document text contains "statistical analysis plan" — … worth confirming.'}
- chain_seq 8, vault.document.file, 300 ms later: from {placementStatus:'suggested'} to {placementStatus:'confirmed'}, by user 1 (Demo Founder).

So the walkthrough's "auto-suggested into Module 5 and then confirmed" is true in the audit chain, but nothing on screen shows it. Two things in code hide it.

(1) The demo seed overrides the product's own wording. When a person clicks "Confirm filing" with no note, server/services/vault/vault-placement.service.ts:210-214 (placementRationale) records "Suggested filing confirmed (<classifier rationale>)." That is exactly the presenter's story. But scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech.mjs:181-189 (ensureFiled) always passes `note`, and line 210 makes that note replace the rationale. The grey line therefore says "by the launch demo seed" and the classifier's proposal is lost from the pane. The same template is used for all six biotech documents.

(2) scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs:130-131 passes `note: "Filed by the MDX demo pack into ${doc.folderId}. ${PROVENANCE}"`. That shows a raw folder id ("k510") and the "no AI provider is configured" provenance sentence on a governed filing record.

A secondary product gap: the History row label is generic. server/routes/audit-trail-ledger.routes.ts:321 maps 'vault.document.file' to "Filing recorded", and auditLogEntry (line 258) reads `reason` only from the row's reason column, which is null here. The from→to change and the rationale in new_values are never shown.

A side mislabel: "Looks like: Protocol" on the SAP comes from server/services/vault/vault-filing.service.ts:219 and :264. Both map SAP to evidence kind 'protocol' because that vocabulary has no SAP kind.

Severity: I would rate this medium, not high. The screen does attribute the filing to a person (Demo Founder) and the record supports the claim. What a client would notice is the seed's wording and the missing suggestion step.

```js

... body: { documentId: hit.id, folderId: spec.folderId, confirm: true, ctdSection: spec.sectionCode,

```

(b) scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/mdx.mjs:129-132. Drop `${PROVENANCE}` and the raw folder id from the note. verdict.cause:
The Data room counts and the source list below them filter different rows, and the difference is the native Quality-record projections.

Commit f4c230dfac (2026-11-06) started writing QMS records into cre_evidence_sources as source_type='client_document' with provenance.origin='native_record_snapshot'. These rows are created by syncQualityProjectSources (record-source.ts:97), which runs on any first-page project catalogue read (data-room-search.ts:134), for example the Evidence step. Each row carries metadata.dossier={evidenceKind:'qms'} and no suggested folder. The commit did not update the stage counter.

1. **The list hides them.** adaptSource forces originalFileAvailable=false for native_record_snapshot (server/services/clinical-regulatory-evidence/evidence-spine.service.ts:1094). The route then drops those rows with `.filter(s => s.dataEligible !== false && s.originalFileAvailable !== false)` (server/routes/c2c/project-vault.ts:1973).
2. **The counter keeps them.** countDataRoomStages (server/services/vault/vault-data-room-filing.ts:96-118) filters only on capturedDataEligibleSql/capturedBinaryAvailableSql (lines 111-112). Those check dispositions and lineage, not origin. So every native row counts as captured, and because has_dossier is true with a null folder and nothing filed, it also counts as "needs review".
3. **The UI prints both without checking they agree.** Vault.tsx:596 prints "Nothing captured for this project yet." whenever sources.length===0, even when captured>0. RoomNotes (Vault.tsx:174-183) prints "N need review".

I confirmed this through the signed-in session's catalogue (GET /api/c2c/projects/:id/sources). C2C-101 holds 15 current sources: one FDA information-request .txt (the only listed source, classified) and 14 qms rows with originalFileAvailable=false. NeuroPanel holds 14, all qms. C2C-201 holds 6, all qms. These match the strip's needsReview numbers exactly (14 / 14 / 6).

"Filed to vault 0" above six Filed uploads is a separate point. The strip counts only data-room captures matched to the Vault by checksum. The six PDFs were uploaded straight into the Vault (vault.documents) and never captured, so 0 is literally correct but reads as a contradiction. The minimal fix below does not change it.

Also confirmed: cross-program change controls in the Evidence catalogue. Both demo change controls appear in all three programs. The seeds create them without programId (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-qms.mjs:89; mdx-qms.mjs:62-72). A change control with no program_id is scoped to the whole organization (project-evidence.ts:267), so it is projected into every program. That is a separate seed defect on the Evidence step.
verdict.minimalFix:
Make the counter use the same rows as the list. In server/services/vault/vault-data-room-filing.ts, in countDataRoomStages's inner WHERE (after line 112, `AND ${capturedDataEligibleSql('s')} AND ${capturedBinaryAvailableSql('s')}`), add:

    AND s.provenance->>'origin' IS DISTINCT FROM 'native_record_snapshot'

You can bind NATIVE_RECORD_ORIGIN from ../clinical-regulatory-evidence/record-source as $3 instead of the literal. Add a comment pointing at evidence-spine.service.ts:1094 and project-vault.ts:1973 so the two definitions stay together. Update the docstring at lines 85-95: "only data-eligible sources whose original file is available, native Quality projections excluded, as the lane's rows exclude them".

Optional defensive UI change: in client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/Vault.tsx:596, change `{block.sources.length === 0 && (` to `{block.sources.length === 0 && (block.captured ?? 0) === 0 && (`. Then the empty-state line can never sit beside a non-zero count.

Proof: add a case to tests/db/data-room-processing.dbtest.ts showing that a current native_record_snapshot row with dossier {evidenceKind:'qms'} is not counted as captured or needs-review. Show it failing before the change.

Expected after the fix:
- C2C-101: "Captured 1 › Classified 1 › Filed to vault 0", "Show 1 source", no "need review" line.
- NeuroPanel and C2C-201: "Captured 0 › Classified 0 › Filed to vault 0" plus "Nothing captured for this project yet."

Both now agree with their lists. countDataRoomStages has one caller (project-vault.ts:2027).

Not covered by this fix:
- **Filed to vault label (copy):** label the strip as data-room captures, not Vault uploads, so "Filed to vault 0" does not read against the six Filed uploads.
- **Seed:** pass programId when the demo seeds create change controls (biotech-qms.mjs:89, mdx-qms.mjs POST body). Then the biotech change control stops appearing in NeuroPanel and vice versa.

No data change is allowed, so steer around the strip:
- Open Vault on C2C-101 only and click "Uploads · 6". Scroll until the "Uploaded files" heading is at the top of the screen before pointing at the six PDFs and their Module filing, so the Data room row is off-screen.

Those have no file to place, so the classifier doesn't propose a folder. The six PDFs were uploaded straight into the Vault, which is why the data-room 'Filed' stage reads 0."
- On the Evidence step, avoid opening the change-control rows: each program shows both programs' change controls.

verdict.cause:
The Audit trail screen fetches only the newest 200 ledger rows and treats that slice as the whole ledger. All filters, search and counts run over the slice, and nothing tells the user it is a slice.

1. The client asks for no limit. client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/AdminSurfaces.tsx:208 calls useLiveRows<AuditEntry>('/api/audit-trail/ledger') with no query parameters.
2. So the server applies its default of 200. server/routes/audit-trail-ledger.routes.ts:747-750 sets limit = min(1000, max(1, parseInt(req.query.limit ?? '200'))). AUDIT_LOGS_SQL (:525-542) orders newest first and applies LIMIT $2. readAuditLedger (:633-648) then cuts the merged list to `limit`. The route accepts only `limit`: no kind filter, no search term, no cursor.
3. The client filters and searches only that slice:
   - the kind filter and search box at AdminSurfaces.tsx:213-224;
   - the kindCounts behind the filter chips at :226-229;
   - the header at :443, which renders `${entries.length} entries — hash-chained` as if it were the total;
   - AnA's context at ~:290-300, which publishes totalEntries: entries.length (200), so AnA would repeat the wrong total.
4. The client has no paging or "load older" control.

Meanwhile the chain banner on the same screen reports the server's whole-chain count (meta.chain.rowsChecked, 593 today). The two numbers contradict each other side by side.

**Why it fails even on a freshly seeded instance.** The demo seed itself writes about 558 rows, from 16:58 to 17:19. The biotech pack is seeded first and the MDX pack after it, and the biotech Protocol Synopsis signatures are among the very first seed rows. They land at about row 530 even with no browsing noise, so this is not an artifact of other agents' traffic. Every document download or preview during the demo adds more rows on top.

- "Point at the newest entries: vault ingest … authoring freeze … QMS approvals … change record" is wrong, because the newest entries are MDX seed rows and live downloads or previews.
- Even after the fix, filtering E-sign would show 18 events, not "the two signature events".

verdict.cause:
Reproduced in a fresh browser. I signed in with Demo access, clicked Biostatistics in the rail, and the default worked example's Sample Size Rationale shows "Effect size: current 0.38, breakpoint 0.361 (5% margin)" and "Attrition rate: current 0.15, breakpoint 0.22499999999999998 (50% margin)". I then clicked "[Demo · Biotech] C2C-101-201 — Phase 2 dose-ranging study in plaque psoriasis", which shows "Effect size: current 0.47, breakpoint 0.4465 (5% margin)" and "Attrition rate: current 0.08, breakpoint 0.12 (50% margin)". No HTTP or page errors.

Root cause is in server/services/ana-biostats/judgment-engine.ts, assessFragility (lines 561-593):

(1) Line 568 uses `approxPower = 1 - normCdf(z_{1-α/2} - mult·z_power)`. That is not a power function. At mult = 0.95 it gives 0.229 for the worked example (α 0.05, power 0.9) and 0.153 for C2C-101-201 (α 0.025, power 0.9). So the loop always stops at its first step and reports a 5% margin for practically every design: it only fails to stop at 0.95 when α is 0.20 and power 0.99. Using the engine's own power formulas, the true powers at the reported breakpoints are 85.9% (Schoenfeld, 184 events, HR 1-0.361) and 86.9% (two-proportion test, n = 22 per group, p1 = 0.08). Neither is below 80%. The true effect-size breakpoints are about 0.338 (11% margin) and about 0.4065 (13.5% margin).

(2) Lines 588-593 hard-code the attrition breakpoint as `Math.min(attritionRate * 1.5, 0.50)` with percentMargin 50. Nothing is computed, and the value is printed unrounded (0.15 × 1.5 = 0.22499999999999998). The computed value `maxAttrition` at line 586 is never used. For the worked example the real breakpoint is about 0.37: 396 enrolled, and 80% power needs about 137 events. The Design Assumption Note at document-generator.ts:373 states this invented figure as "50% margin before power drops below threshold".

The values are rendered verbatim at document-generator.ts:245 (Sample Size Rationale) and :363/:373 (Design Assumption Note), under a footer that says "All numeric results are deterministic". They also reach sme-router.ts:253 and the role explanation at judgment-engine.ts:888.

Two of the reporter's downstream claims are overstated:
- The confidence score (assessConfidence, around lines 802-843) does not read fragility at all.
- The fragility index shown for these two seeded designs (40 and 30) does not change, because their true margins (11% and 13.5%) are still under the 20% threshold at line 600. The +25 only inflates designs whose true margin is 20% or more, such as α 0.05 with 95% power (true margin about 22%). Through deriveOverallRisk (lines 788-795) that can raise the risk level.

Severity: the screen is not on either walkthrough (docs/demo/*.md never mention Biostatistics), but it is a rail work area. The float artifact and the false 5% / 50% margins are visible on its landing document and on the seeded C2C-101-201 design. I rate it medium-to-high rather than a blocker.
verdict.minimalFix:
Edit server/services/ana-biostats/judgment-engine.ts, assessFragility, lines 563-593:

(a) Effect size. Hoist `const zA = this.normQuantile(1 - input.alpha / 2); const zB = this.normQuantile(input.powerTarget);`. Replace the loop at lines 566-574 with an integer-percent loop, `for (let pct = 99; pct > 30; pct -= 1) { const mult = pct / 100; const approxPower = this.normCdf(mult * (zA + zB) - zA); if (approxPower < 0.80) { breakpointEffect = baseEffect * mult; break; } }`. The formula is power at a reduced effect with N fixed, which is the normal approximation linear in effect size: exact for continuous endpoints, close for binary and log-rank. The integer step also removes the 0.05 float drift. A more exact follow-up is to make ComputationEngine.estimatePowerAtN (computation-engine.ts:1067) public and call it with `{...input, effectSize: baseEffect*mult}` at `comp.sampleSize.total`.

(b) Attrition. Replace the hard-coded block at lines 586-594 with a computed breakpoint: `const adj = comp.adjustedTotal ?? comp.sampleSize.total; const k = ((zA + this.normQuantile(0.80)) / (zA + zB)) ** 2; const aBreak = 1 - comp.sampleSize.total * k / adj;`. Push the entry only when `input.attritionRate > 0 && aBreak > input.attritionRate`, with `breakpointValue: Number(aBreak.toFixed(3))` and `percentMargin: Number(((aBreak / input.attritionRate - 1) * 100).toFixed(1))`. Delete the unused `maxAttrition` at line 586.

If (b) is too much for today, delete the attrition push entirely rather than print an invented breakpoint.

Optional hardening: in document-generator.ts:245/:363/:373, format with `Number(sp.breakpointValue.toFixed(3))`.

Add a unit test that fails today. For the worked-example input it should assert an effect-size percentMargin of at least 10 and an attrition breakpointValue other than 1.5 × attrition.
verdict.demoWorkaround: On the Biostatistics screen, do not scroll the Sample Size Rationale down to "Statistical Assessment / Sensitivity Points" (on both the default worked example and C2C-101-201), and do not open the Design Assumption Note document. Stop at Result and Scenario Analysis, which are computed correctly (for example 396 subjects at 90.0% power; 72 at 90.2%). If a client biostatistician asks about fragility or sensitivity, say the breakpoint heuristic is being recalibrated, and that a 5% loss of effect leaves about 86% power, not below 80%.
