I reproduced it in a fresh session. Steps: Demo access, then rail Reporting & analytics, then the C2C-101 card in the main pane, then the "Compare readiness across all my projects" chip. The C2C-101 portfolio card reads "missing · critical risk · 23 critical blockers / No governed artifacts discovered for this scope / No approved or locked governed artifacts / Administrative Forms: ...". The server returns exactly that in GET /api/insights-canvas/overview?programId=7f7bc7b2-... (portfolio.programs[0].topBlockers).

Root cause: the portfolio card shows `computed.blockers.slice(0, 3)` (server/services/report-os/portfolio/fetch.ts:90) from computeInitialRun. Its first two blockers are hard-coded artifact-store checks in server/services/report-os/orchestrator.ts:110-114 ("No governed artifacts discovered for this scope") and :131-142 ("No approved or locked governed artifacts"). Both count only concept2cure_artifacts rows: AnA drafts, CMC-composed Module 3 sections and imported files. C2C-101's demo content lives in other stores: 12 authoring documents (Protocol Synopsis FROZEN, Module 2.5 IN_REVIEW, SOP-001/002 APPROVED), 6 Vault uploads, and sequence 0000. So the store holds 0 rows for project 1. C2C-201 has rows from the CMC compile, so its card drops the first line. Side by side, the flagship program looks emptier than the side program. The card gives no definition of the term. A buyer who just saw a Frozen synopsis and Approved SOPs on Project home reads "No approved or locked governed artifacts" as false. verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session. Steps: Demo access, then the rail's 'CMC / Module 3', then the C2C-201 card (it lands on project-home), then the 'CMC / Module 3' work area, then 'Study records', then the 'Stability' tab. The header reads '3 active studies · 14 outside limits'. The red banner reads '14 stability results are outside the acceptance criteria — Assay at 0 mo (99.8), Assay at 6 mo (99.4), Assay at 12 mo (99.1) and 11 more'. The studies read '6 recorded · 6 OOS', '5 recorded · 5 OOS' and '3 recorded · 3 OOS'. When the drug-substance study is expanded, 99.8 against '98.0 - 102.0 %' is marked OOS. Shelf-life evidence reads '0 within acceptance criteria, 14 outside', with 0/6, 0/5 and 0/3.

Root cause: the register and the composed dossier use two different verdict sources.
- The register (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/CmcModule.tsx) decides OOS only from a self-declared boolean on each result. It treats a missing flag as out of specification:
  - :1786 `const oos = allResults.filter((r) => !r.withinSpecification);` feeds the header (:2037), the banner (:2039-2046) and the shelf-life summary (:2180);
  - :2087 does the same for the per-study 'N OOS' count;
  - :2137-2138 renders the chip `x.withinSpecification ? 'within' : 'OOS'`;
  - :2189 does the same for the 'Within limits' n/N.
- The server never requires the flag. stability_data is an untyped json column (shared/schema.ts:3751), and GET /api/cmc/stability-studies (server/api/cmc/routes.ts:554-596) returns it as stored. The Module 3 composer ignores the flag and computes the verdict from the value and the criterion (server/services/module3Composer.ts:384 `pointVerdict`, using parseNumeric and parseAcceptanceCriterion from server/services/cmc/recorded-stability.ts:90/209).
- The C2C-201 seed (scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-work-content.mjs:221-260) records its 14 results with a value and a specification but no `withinSpecification`. The captured API payload confirms 0 of the 14 results carry the field.

So every C2C-201 result is labelled OOS, while the composed §3.2.S.7 says all 6 are within and §3.2.P.8 names exactly one (Total impurities at 6 months, 0.61 against NMT 0.5 %). The control case confirms the mechanism: C2C-101, whose seed sets `withinSpecification: true` (biotech-work-content.mjs:114-127), shows '2 active studies · 0 outside limits'.

The same split has a second effect. The result form defaults 'Within specification' to 'yes' (cmcRegisterForms.ts:472). A person who records 0.61 against NMT 0.5 % without changing it gets a register that says 'within' while the dossier says OUTSIDE.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser session: Demo access, then the rail's CMC / Module 3, then the "[Demo · Biotech] C2C-201 oral JAK1 inhibitor" program, then Overview > Section approvals > row 3.1 (100%, Draft) > "Approve section". The "Read before you sign — 21 CFR §11.50" panel reads "The drug substance is C2C-201 tablets. The drug product is formulated as a Film-coated tablet." Row 3.3 (100%) reads "for the drug substance (C2C-201 tablets) and drug product (Film-coated tablet)". GET /api/cmc/module3-os/sections/<project>/3.1 returns the same stored narrative, so the text comes from the server, not the client.

Root cause, in server/services/module3Composer.ts:
- The section rules for 3.1 and 3.3 (lines 217-218) take sources from both `drug_substance` and `drug_product`.
- Both source types carry a field called `name`. The write-through mapper sets it from substanceName for the substance and from productName for the product (server/services/cmc-write-through.ts:221 and :305).
- The '3.1' generator (line 3126) and the '3.3' generator (line 3161) both read `val(m, 'name')`, and val() returns the first source that has the field.
- Sources load newest first (`ORDER BY updated_at DESC` in loadCanonicalSources, server/services/cmc/module3-compile.ts:44-51). The seed writes the product ('C2C-201 tablets', scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-work-content.mjs:188) after the substance ('C2C-201', line 170), so the product's name is labelled "the drug substance".

I confirmed the order dependence by running the composer directly with tsx:
- product newest: "The drug substance is C2C-201 tablets."
- substance newest: "The drug substance is C2C-201."

The same check exposed a second problem: with a substance that has no name, §3.1 still reports 100% and nothing missing, because the required `name` field is counted across both source types and the product's name satisfies it.

The table-of-contents part of the finding is also true. The 3.1 table lists only 3.2.S.1-7 and 3.2.P.1-8. Its comment (lines 3152-3154) says 3.2.A and 3.2.R are listed by module3-extensions.ts, but no code there adds anything to the 3.1 table. Meanwhile 3.2.A.1-3, 3.2.R.1.US and 3.3 are all composed and shown for this project.

The "drug_product:2, drug_substance:2" lineage text is the raw source_key (type:id), rendered at client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/CmcModule.tsx:481. It is jargon, but not wrong.

Severity: no line in docs/demo/biotech-walkthrough.md covers C2C-201 section approvals. So this is not on the scripted path, but it is on a likely-clicked path in a featured work area. A CMC reviewer at a regulated buyer would catch "drug substance is ... tablets" at once, on the first section, marked 100% complete, with "Sign & approve" active.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this from a fresh browser session at trunk 32a0a657a9. Path: Demo access, then rail CMC / Module 3, then the C2C-201 project card, then Study records, then the Specifications tab, then the QC testing card.

**QC testing card**
- The header reads "5 samples — 4 pass / 0 fail — 5 awaiting review".
- Row DS-2502-R2 shows 97.4 % against 98.0 - 102.0 % with a green "Pass" chip. Nothing on the page says it is outside its criterion.
- The API row carries `testResults.observation` = "retest requested; investigation INV-2026-014 open". The register never shows it: neither the row nor the page contains INV-2026-014.
- I opened Review on DS-2502-R2 and cancelled. The dialog does not show the result, the criterion or the observation, and its Disposition control is preset to "pass".

**Batch records tab**
- C2C201-DS-2502 shows Eligible "Yes" with an enabled Release button.
- I opened the "Release batch C2C201-DS-2502" e-signature drawer and cancelled. It offers approved, conditional and rejected.
- C2C201-DP-2503 also shows "Yes", although none of its results is reviewed.

**Why it happens**
1. The only check of a result against its criterion is `qcResultVerdict`, which is private to `server/services/module3Composer.ts:893-919`. Only the composed §3.2.S.4.4 / §3.2.P.5.4 tables use it.
2. The register counts and colours the typed field alone:
   - `client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/cmcRegisters.tsx:727-728` builds the pass/fail counts from `passFailStatus` only.
   - `:770` renders `chip(r.passFailStatus)`.
   - `qcResultValue` (`:703-707`) drops `testResults.observation`.
   - `GET /api/cmc/qc-testing` (`server/api/cmc/routes.ts:742-758`) is a bare `db.select()` with no computed verdict.
3. Batch eligibility is a client rule about deviations only: `client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/CmcModule.tsx:2533` `const eligible = (r) => r.dev === 0`, used at `:2614` and `:2616`. The card subtitle at `:2601` says release is "over the batch's recorded, reviewed QC results".
4. The server release gate has the same gap. `server/services/cmc/batch-release-evidence.ts:92` sets `passed: passFail === 'pass' || passFail === 'passed'` from the declared field only. So `evaluateRecordedRelease` would refuse a full ("approved") release of C2C201-DS-2502 only because its two results are unreviewed. It would accept a §11-signed **conditional** release: no open deviation and no declared fail. That would put a signature over a batch whose own assay result is out of specification. I did not complete that act (not allowed); this conclusion comes from the code.

**The seed is deliberate**
`scripts/demo/launch-demo/packs/biotech-work-content.mjs:259-268` plants DS-2502-R2 as a declared pass over a failing result so the composer's contradiction shows. Only the composer reads it that way.

The walkthroughs never send the presenter to Batch records or QC testing (`biotech-walkthrough.md` mentions CMC only at line 44), so no script line is contradicted. It is still a wrong, misleading state on a featured work area.
verdict.minimalFix: Five changes, ordered by importance. verified.title: Each failed AnA turn trips a circuit breaker that blocks every AnA read for 30 s
verified.steps: Ask AnA anything (e.g. Home composer: 'Which C2C-201 batches are pending release?'), then within 30 s ask a follow-up in the same thread ('And which QC result contradicts its disposition?'), or open any AnA panel.
verified.observed: The first answer is honest: 'No AI provider is configured for this deployment, so AnA cannot answer…'. The second, within 30 s, becomes the generic 'AnA couldn't complete this request. Try again, or ask an administrator for help if it keeps happening.' The Progress side panel shows a red 'Background — Couldn't read the background queue. Retry'. Server log: '[circuit-breaker-middleware:ai-service] Circuit open, fast failing request'. GET /api/ana-ri/agent-activity and /api/ana-ri/runs?mine=live return 503 {status:'circuit_open'}. The middleware counts every 5xx, including the honest 503 GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE, and never closes again on success: after the 10th cumulative failure since boot, every further AnA attempt reopens it for 30 s, server-wide (it also affects other users).
verified.expected: An unconfigured provider is a refusal, not a failure. It should not trip a breaker, and non-model reads (activity, runs, memory) should never sit behind the AI breaker. The second question should get the same honest message.

verdict.cause:
I reproduced this in a fresh browser: signed in through Demo access, clicked Home in the rail, and asked a question in the Home composer.

What happens on the server:
- `/api/ana-ri` is mounted behind the shared `ai-service` circuit breaker (`server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:35`). That covers the whole router: the model stream and also plain reads such as `agent-activity`, `runs`, `threads`, `memory` and `live-drive/state`.
- The breaker middleware counts every response with status 500 or above as a failure (`server/middleware/circuitBreaker.ts:342-348`). That includes the deliberate, honest refusal `sendError(res, 503, 'No AI providers available.', null, 'GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE')` in `server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1037-1040`.
- The failure count only goes up. Nothing on the middleware path resets it or closes the breaker after a success:
  - `close()` runs only from `allowSingleRequest` (`:121-124`, the `execute()` path, which the middleware never calls) and from `reset()` (`:285-288`).
  - So once the breaker goes HALF_OPEN after 30 s it stays there while 2xx responses keep arriving. With the count already at or above the threshold of 10 (`server/startup/routes.ts:71-77`), the next 5xx calls `open()` again (`:189-191`).
- The result: from the 10th 5xx since boot onward, every unanswered AnA question blocks all `/api/ana-ri/*`, `/api/ai` and `/api/ai-assistance` routes with `503 {status:'circuit_open'}` for 30 s, for every user on the server.

What the user sees:
- The client has no mapping for `circuit_open`. `streamRefusalText` in `client/src/concept2cure/components/ana/useAnaChat.ts:675` falls through to the generic "AnA couldn't complete this request…".
- The work dock's agent-activity read fails, so it shows the red "Couldn't read the background queue. Retry" (`client/src/concept2cure/v2/AnaWorkSections.tsx:271`). This appears right after the first question, because that question's 503 opens the breaker before the panel reads.

This is not just this machine's setup. Both presenter scripts say the demo runs with no AI provider configured (`docs/demo/mdx-walkthrough.md:12-15` and `:196-199`, `docs/demo/biotech-walkthrough.md:118`), so the demo configuration itself takes this path. With a provider configured the stream answers 200 over SSE and the defect is mostly hidden, but the count still never goes down, so any 10 pre-stream 5xx errors over the server's lifetime arm it. Severity high stands.
verdict.minimalFix:
Two changes, both small, to existing files:

1. `server/middleware/circuitBreaker.ts`
   - In class `CircuitBreaker`, add a public method:
     `recordSuccess() { if (this.state === CircuitState.HALF_OPEN) { this.close(); this.processQueue(); } else if (this.state === CircuitState.CLOSED) { this.failures = 0; } }`
   - Replace the `finish` handler at lines 342-348 with:
     `res.on('finish', () => { if (res.statusCode >= 500) { if (!res.locals?.circuitBreakerExempt) breaker.recordFailure(new Error(`Server error ${res.statusCode} on ${req.method} ${req.path}`)); } else { breaker.recordSuccess(); } });`
   - This changes the count from "failures ever" to "consecutive failures", and it lets HALF_OPEN close again on a success.

2. `server/routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1038-1039`
   - Inside the `if (!gw || …)` block, add `res.locals.circuitBreakerExempt = true;` just before `return sendError(res, 503, 'No AI providers available.', null, 'GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE');`.
   - An unconfigured provider is a configuration refusal, not an upstream fault.

Add two cases to `server/middleware/__tests__/circuitBreaker.test.ts`:
- 5xx, then 2xx, then 5xx with threshold 2 stays CLOSED;
- an exempt 503 is not counted.

Each new test should be seen failing before the fix.

Optional, slightly larger, separate change: in `server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:35`, wrap the breaker so reads never sit behind it, for example `(req, res, next) => (req.method === 'GET' ? next() : aiCircuitBreaker(req, res, next))`. You could also map `status === 'circuit_open'` to its own sentence in `streamRefusalText` (`useAnaChat.ts`, around line 675) instead of the generic fallback.
verdict.demoWorkaround:
The failure count lives only in server memory. It is at 14 now on the running server (pid 5039, booted 17:12:31), so every AnA question trips the breaker.

1. Restart the demo server just before 1:00 pm, and make sure no one rehearses AnA questions on it afterwards. A fresh boot allows 9 unanswered questions before the breaker can trip.
2. During the demo:
   - Wait at least 30 seconds between AnA questions. I confirmed a question asked 33 s later gets the honest "No AI provider is configured…" message again.
   - Keep the Progress side panel closed right after a question.
   - If the red "Couldn't read the background queue" appears, wait 30 s and click Retry. It then reads correctly.
3. Simplest of all: do not ask AnA live. Say what the walkthrough already says: no AI provider is configured for this demo, and the numbers come from deterministic engines.

presenterAdvice: The walkthroughs have no CMC or AnA step, so this part is improvised. Keep it short and use C2C-201 (rail CMC / Module 3 → C2C-201 card → Work areas 'CMC / Module 3').

Best moment: Overview → Section approvals → row 3.2.P.8 → 'Approve section'. This opens a read-only panel ('Read before you sign'). It shows the composed stability section naming the one OOS result (total impurities 0.61 % at 6 months accelerated) and withholding the shelf-life conclusion. Say 'this is what a signer reads', then click Cancel. Do not dwell on its narrative: it describes only the accelerated condition, and it repeats a false 'more than one storage condition' sentence.

Do NOT open Study records → Stability. The red banner claims all 14 results are OOS, including 99.8 % against 98–102 %. If someone opens it, say the register flag is wrong and that the composed §3.2.P.8 (one OOS) is the engine's verdict.

Avoid the QC testing table and Batch records: DS-2502-R2 (97.4 % against 98.0–102.0 %) shows 'Pass' and the batch 'Eligible: Yes'. The composed §3.2.S.4 states that contradiction, but it cannot be opened from CMC.

Do not open §3.1 (it says 'The drug substance is C2C-201 tablets'), §3.2.S.3 ('confirmed by [methods not specified]') or §3.2.P.2 (boilerplate claim). §3.2.A.2 (adventitious agents) and §3.2.S.1 read cleanly.
Show the honest boundary on C2C-101: Module 3 build refuses a biologic and names ICH Q6B / Q5A(R2) / Q5C. Stay on the build tab: the Overview and QbD tabs around it are inconsistent.
Avoid History (raw JSON, 'by 1'), Evidence (record keys and UUIDs) and the Approvals & audit 'Actor 1' column.

Do NOT click Build, Compile Module 3, Run contradiction sweep, Check export gate, Release, Record review, or 'Create working copy': they write governed records. 'Run ICH compliance check' is read-only and deterministic, but its Q2 warnings contradict the 'Validated' methods, so skip it unless asked.

AnA has no model provider here. Ask at most ONE question in the whole demo. The honest answer appears in about 2 s: 'No AI provider is configured for this deployment, so AnA cannot answer. This is a server setting, not your connection.' Say that is by design: AnA refuses rather than fabricates, and numbers come from the engines.

Never send a second AnA question, or click another AnA chip and send it, within 30 seconds. A server circuit breaker turns the reply into a generic 'AnA couldn't complete this request…' and shows a red 'Couldn't read the background queue' in the side panel.
AnA chips (project page, CMC tabs) only fill the composer; nothing happens until you press Send. Do not click 'Demos', 'Advance the next section' or 'Ask AnA to propose it': they all need the model.
The question is not kept: the project's 'Conversations' and the rail's Recents stay empty afterwards. Do not promise that the conversation is saved.
